Estimates and contrasts of fixed (and random) effects

Source: R/estimates.R
vlm_estimate.Rd

vlm_estimate() gives estimates of linear combinations \(\mathbf{l}^{\top}\boldsymbol{\beta}\) (the ESTIMATE statement of SAS PROC MIXED), optionally including random effects \(\mathbf{k}^{\top}\mathbf{u}\) (the narrow or intermediate inference space). vlm_contrast() gives F tests of sets of linear combinations \(\mathbf{L}\boldsymbol{\beta} = \mathbf{0}\) (the CONTRAST statement).

Usage

vlm_estimate(fit, L, random = NULL, level = 0.95)

# Default S3 method
vlm_estimate(fit, L, random = NULL, level = 0.95)

vlm_contrast(fit, L)

# Default S3 method
vlm_contrast(fit, L)

Arguments

fit

a result of vlm_fit().

L

for vlm_estimate(): a named list of estimates, each a named list of effect coefficients (such as list(Drug = c(-1, 1), "Drug:dose" = c(-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5))) or a numeric vector over all columns of the solution. For vlm_contrast(): a named list of contrasts, each one such row or a list of rows.

random

optional named list (names as in L) of random-effect coefficients for the narrow inference space: each a named list of random effects (as in the effect column of vlm_blup()) with coefficients over their levels.

level

confidence level (default 0.95).

Value

A list of class c("vlm_estimate", "vlm_result", "list") with estimates (label, estimate, standard error, df, t, p, confidence limits and inference space) and L; or of class c("vlm_contrast", "vlm_result", "list") with contrasts (label, numerator and denominator df, F and p).

Details

Coefficients are given per effect as in SAS, in the order of the levels in the solution table (fit$fixed); missing trailing coefficients are zero. The variance of an estimate is \(\mathbf{l}^{\top}\mathbf{C}_{11}\mathbf{l} + 2\mathbf{l}^{\top}\mathbf{C}_{12}\mathbf{k} + \mathbf{k}^{\top}\mathbf{C}_{22}\mathbf{k}\), where \(\mathbf{C}_{11} = (\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{V}^{-1} \mathbf{X})^{-}\), \(\mathbf{C}_{12} = -\mathbf{C}_{11}\mathbf{X}^{\top}\mathbf{V}^{-1}\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{G}\) and \(\mathbf{C}_{22} = \mathbf{G} - \mathbf{G}\mathbf{Z}^{\top}\mathbf{P}\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{G}\) (Henderson's mixed model equations). The F statistic of a contrast is $$F = \frac{(\mathbf{L}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}})^{\top}(\mathbf{L}\mathbf{C}_{11}\mathbf{L}^{\top})^{-1} (\mathbf{L}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}})}{\mathrm{rank}(\mathbf{L})},$$ with the denominator degrees of freedom of the fit. Rows that are not estimable give NA.

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi. Sections 2.5 and 2.6.

McLean, R. A., Sanders, W. L. and Stroup, W. W. (1991). A unified approach to mixed linear models. The American Statistician, 45, 54-64.

See also

vlm_lsmeans, vlm_fit

Other VetResearchLMM inference: emmeans_mixed_model(), report_mixed_model(), vlm_blup(), vlm_lsmeans()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "satterth"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
# Example 2.5.3.1: ESTIMATE statements (levels: Drug BERENIL samorin, dose h l)
es <-
  vlm_estimate(
      fit    = fm
    , L      = list(
          "drug dif"     = list(Drug = c(-1, 1), "Drug:dose" = c(-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
        , "Samorin mean" = list(Intercept = 1, Drug = c(0, 1),
                                dose = c(0.5, 0.5), "Drug:dose" = c(0, 0, 0.5, 0.5))
        , "Samorin HvsL" = list(dose = c(1, -1), "Drug:dose" = c(0, 0, 1, -1))
        , "Samorin high" = list(Intercept = 1, Drug = c(0, 1),
                                dose = c(1, 0), "Drug:dose" = c(0, 0, 1, 0))
        )
    , random = NULL
    , level  = 0.95
    )
es
#> Estimates (denominator df: satterth)
#> 
#> Estimates
#>         label estimate     se    df      t        p  lower  upper space
#>      drug dif   -5.558 0.6917 5.000 -8.036 0.000483 -7.336 -3.780 broad
#>  Samorin mean    19.31  1.048 6.205  18.43  < 1e-04  16.77  21.85 broad
#>  Samorin HvsL    4.350 0.8359 10.00  5.204 0.000399  2.487  6.213 broad
#>  Samorin high    21.48  1.128 8.208  19.05  < 1e-04  18.89  24.07 broad
#> 
#> Sources: Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998); McLean, Sanders and Stroup
#> (1991); Satterthwaite (1946); Giesbrecht and Burns (1985); Fai and Cornelius
#> (1996). Full references: vlm_cite(x).

# Example 2.6.1: CONTRAST statements
ct <-
  vlm_contrast(
      fit = fm
    , L   = list(
          "drug dif" = list(Drug = c(-1, 1), "Drug:dose" = c(-0.5, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
        , "all"      = list(
              list(Drug = c(1, -1), "Drug:dose" = c(0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5))
            , list(dose = c(1, -1), "Drug:dose" = c(0.5, -0.5, 0.5, -0.5))
            , list("Drug:dose" = c(0.5, -0.5, -0.5, 0.5))
            )
        )
    )
ct
#> Contrasts (denominator df: satterth)
#> 
#> Contrasts
#>     label num_df den_df     F        p
#>  drug dif      1  5.000 64.58 0.000483
#>       all      3  7.143 31.20 0.000179
#> 
#> Sources: Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998); McLean, Sanders and Stroup
#> (1991); Satterthwaite (1946); Giesbrecht and Burns (1985); Fai and Cornelius
#> (1996). Full references: vlm_cite(x).
